elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor." The conforming edit to 2.1 ("without reduction rights, subject to Section 9.4") removes the prior denial of termination rights, so the new right is not contradicted by the take-or-pay commitment.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor" — 30 days, written, and no additional condition or consent requirement.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Retained 10.2 says only "Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination." A refund covering the post-termination period is not a pro-rata refund, and the refund is limited to "recurring" Fees rather than prepaid Fees generally (Fees as defined also include professional services, usage and other amounts). No pro-rata refund language was added to the new convenience clause.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Vendor may not terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term." Sections 9.1–9.3 give Vendor only for-cause/insolvency rights, so no residual Vendor convenience right exists mid-term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The drafted notice period is thirty days, which is outside the literal 60–90 day fallback band (it is more favourable to us, but this fallback checklist element is not literally satisfied; completeness should be pursued at the preferred level instead).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee, exit charge or liquidated payment is imposed anywhere in the cited termination provisions, and 2.1's take-or-pay commitment is now expressly "subject to Section 9.4," so no fee cap is needed.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Vendor is barred from convenience termination "during a committed term" and Sections 9.1–9.3 grant Vendor only cause-based rights, so no mid-term Vendor convenience exit survives.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence prohibits Vendor convenience termination during a committed term but sets no notice period for any Vendor convenience termination outside a committed term; no 90-day (or any) Vendor notice obligation appears in the operative text.

reasons: Position is not complete at either level. At the preferred level the only gap is the refund element: retained 10.2 refunds "prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination," which is neither expressly pro rata nor coextensive with prepaid Fees as defined (it excludes prepaid professional services, usage and other amounts). Repair in operative language by adding to the new convenience clause: "in which case Vendor shall refund, on a pro rata basis, all prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination."

Fallback level fails on two elements as literally stated: the drafted notice is 30 days rather than 60–90 days, and no Vendor convenience-termination notice period (90 days) is specified for any period outside a committed term. Because the preferred level needs only the refund fix, pursue completion at the preferred level rather than reworking to the fallback.

Drafting defect to fix: the inserted paragraph carries no section number in the rendered text while amended 2.1 now says "subject to Section 9.4." Number the inserted clause "9.4" expressly so the cross-reference resolves; as rendered it is only inferable from its placement between 9.3 and 9.5.

Minimality is acceptable: the insertion is concise, correctly omits the model language's "in whole or in part" surplus (no partial-termination structure requires it), and adds no survival tail, expense or procedure extras. The 2.1 edit both deletes "or termination" and adds "subject to Section 9.4"; either move alone would cure the contradiction, so the belt-and-braces pairing is mildly redundant but stays within the conforming change needed, and the Customer-favourable "without reduction" restriction is retained.

Intent is preserved: cause-based rights (9.1–9.3), the non-cascading Order Form rule and cumulative-remedies sentence (9.5), and the 10.2 deliverable/refund mechanics all survive without contradiction; the only residual risk is the unnumbered inserted clause noted above.
